title: KSP DAPPA — 3-minute demo (Round 2)
provenance: Every claim below was verified against the live Development deployment on 2026-08-28/29. Numbers come from GET /healthz, GET /meta/services, docs/benchmarks/*.json and docs/capability_counts.json — not from memory. The Round-1 script (rendered 2026-07-26) is superseded; see changes_from_round1 for every line that changed and why.
render_note: This is the narration + shot list. The rendered Round-1 cut (video/out/KSP_DAPPA_Demo_3min.mp4) predates the officer tiers, face identification, the action loop and CSV ingest, and still says 'Hindi' and 'Circuits' — both of which are now false. Re-render before submission.

scenes.visual: Higgsfield b-roll — police records room at night
scenes.text: Across Karnataka, crime records sit in silos. An offender changes one letter of his name, crosses a district line, and disappears.
KSP DAPPA turns forty-five thousand FIR records — on the official Karnataka Police schema — into one intelligence hub, built end to end on Zoho Catalyst.
scenes.lower_third: KSP DAPPA — From Records to Foresight

scenes.visual: Screen: tier switcher walking State → District → Station → Beat, ending on #/beat at phone width
scenes.text: One app, four ranks. A DGP sees all thirty-eight units. A station officer sees this week against the usual. A head constable sees one card: what changed on my beat, what needs attention, what to do tonight — in plain words.
scenes.lower_third: DGP to head constable — one app, four shapes

scenes.visual: Screen #/ — command dashboard, then #/map hotspot fly-to and the month scrubber
scenes.text: Anomaly districts pulse red. Where a number isn't trustworthy we print a dash, not a guess. Press play, and months of crime drift across Karnataka.
scenes.lower_third: A dash, not a wrong number

scenes.visual: Screen #/network — co-accused graph, then an Offender-360 alias panel
scenes.text: The network explorer maps who offends together — twenty-three thousand co-accused links. And the alias matcher's measured precision is printed on the screen that uses it.

scenes.visual: Screen #/identify — upload, quality gate, shortlist, ranked candidates with confidence bars and the audit banner
scenes.text: Face identification, done properly. Zia compares two faces; we never sweep a gallery. Filters narrow to twenty-five candidates, every result carries a confidence figure, and below the floor the answer is no reliable match. Every search needs a case number and a legal basis. Every search is logged.

scenes.visual: Screen #/alerts — open an alert, record a decision with a reason, then the 'what happened to past alerts' panel
scenes.text: An officer acknowledges, assigns or dismisses an alert — a dismissal needs a reason — and the decision is written to the Data Store. Below: what happened to every past alert. How many were real. How long they took.
scenes.lower_third: It records what the officer decided

scenes.visual: Screen #/ingest — pick CaseMaster, drop the 200-row CSV, mapped preview with per-cell marks, rejection report, 'what changed' card
scenes.text: Drop in a CSV in the official format. Every row is checked — the eighteen-digit crime number, the district a coordinate really falls in, the caste column accepted for fidelity and never used. Bad rows come back as a report.

scenes.visual: Screen #/copilot — a plain-language question answering with a chart and the ZCQL it ran; then the Kannada flip
scenes.text: Ask in plain language, or out loud. A chart answers, and shows the query behind it. Then the interface turns Kannada. ಇದು ಕರ್ನಾಟಕಕ್ಕಾಗಿ.
scenes.lower_third: English · ಕನ್ನಡ · every answer shows its query

scenes.visual: Screen #/about — the service matrix and the honesty ledger, scrolling
scenes.text: One Catalyst project, end to end. Thirty-five services, each stating what it does and what it still needs. Every AI answer names the engine behind it — even when that engine was our own fallback.
scenes.lower_third: 35 services, each with an honest status

scenes.text: Today, synthetic FIRs; tomorrow, real CCTNS exports through the same screen. The decisions officers record today are the labels the models learn tomorrow.
KSP DAPPA never tells an officer what to do. It shows what it found, how sure it is, and records what they decided.

changes_from_round1.was: the interface switches to Kannada or Hindi, instantly … lower third 'English · ಕನ್ನಡ · हिंदी'
changes_from_round1.why: BLOCKING TRUTH FIX. The Hindi locale was retired in commit 194bdd1 (decision D-008): Karnataka police work happens in Kannada and English, and an unmaintained third language reads as decoration. The old line would be contradicted by the language switcher on screen.

changes_from_round1.now: cut; Job Scheduling named in the services scene instead
changes_from_round1.why: BLOCKING TRUTH FIX. Catalyst documents Circuits as unavailable to IN-data-centre users and this project runs on .catalystserverless.in (decision D-019). The nightly chain runs as the dappa_nightly cron function with a Job Scheduling pool.

changes_from_round1.was: Ask DAPPA out loud, in Kannada. (as a future item)
changes_from_round1.why: Read-aloud and voice input ship via the browser Web Speech API (decision D-014). It is present tense now, and the roadmap line would understate the build.

changes_from_round1.was: forty-five thousand records; Stratus holds every brief; QuickML and Zia answer the AI calls
changes_from_round1.now: thirty-five services are mapped, and every row states what it is doing and what it still needs
changes_from_round1.why: The service map grew from 28 to 35 rows in Round 2 and now carries a distinct 'unavailable' status for services the IN data centre does not offer. The scene now sells the honesty of the matrix, which is the defensible claim, rather than a service list a judge could tick off against /meta/services.

Officer tiers are the highest-scoring requirement of the Round-2 brief ('usable by a head constable as well as a DGP') and there was no beat in the Round-1 cut. The tier switcher is also the single most demonstrable thing on screen.

Face identification did not exist in Round 1. The narration deliberately leads with the constraints (no sweep, a cap, a floor, a purpose binding, an audit) rather than the capability, because that is what makes it defensible to a police jury.
The action loop converts the dashboard into a system, and 'what happened to past alerts' is the single most persuasive screen for a police evaluator. Round 1 had no write path at all.
CSV ingest is what moves DAPPA from an impressive demo to a pilot candidate; the Round-2 brief calls out that twenty seconds of it outscores fifty features nobody opens.

changes_from_round1.was: the aliases no spreadsheet could join
changes_from_round1.now: the alias matcher's measured precision is published on the screen that uses it
changes_from_round1.why: The measured identity-resolution precision is 0.032 at the deployed threshold (docs/benchmarks/identity_metrics.json). Claiming the joins are a triumph would be contradicted by our own published number; claiming the publication is the triumph is both true and stronger.

changes_from_round1.was: Built end to end on Zoho Catalyst, for the KSP Datathon twenty twenty-six.
changes_from_round1.now: It never tells an officer what to do. It shows what it found, how sure it is, and records what they decided.
changes_from_round1.why: The Round-2 brief names this as the closing line and it is the correct posture on predictive policing; the Catalyst claim is already made in scene 2 and scene 10.

shot_capture_notes: Scenes 3-9 are screen captures of the live Development deployment (https://project-rainfall-60079891305.development.catalystserverless.in/app/index.html). Record scene 3's beat card at 360x640 device emulation so the phone framing is real, not a scaled desktop.
Scene 6: use the Identify screen's 'Use a sample capture' control so no real photograph is ever on camera, and hold on the synthetic-gallery banner for at least one second.
Scene 7: record against the live deployment AFTER the ActionLog seed has been imported, otherwise the outcomes panel is legitimately empty.
Scene 8: the bundled 200-row file is data/ingest_demo/CaseMaster_sample.csv — 12 rows are deliberately broken so the rejection report has something to show.
Keep the Chrome network tab out of shot except where the Round-1 cut used it; the basemap tile requests are declared in the README but do not need airtime.
trim_note: Narration is 370 words. At Charon's measured ~1.94 words/sec that is ~191 s of voice; the Round-1 mix closed its last few seconds with a 1.03x atempo, which brings this to ~185 s against the 178 s ceiling. Scenes 3, 6, 7 and 8 are the Round-2 differentiators and were protected during the trim. If a VO pass still overruns: cut scene 4's second sentence, then scene 11's second sentence, then scene 5's second sentence — in that order, each is restated elsewhere on screen.
